_schema.description: Curated geopolitical event registry per docs/019_Geopolitical_Intelligence.md. Every event must carry sources (invariant: no unverified data). severity and oil_supply_impact are 0-10; confidence is 0-1. status: active | monitoring | resolved. Resolved events are kept forever (invariant: historical information must remain preserved).

events.description: Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz 2026-02-28; re-closed 2026-07-13. As of 07-19: third consecutive day of US-Iran fighting. Trump said he would reimpose the US naval blockade on Iranian ships only and demanded other transiting ships pay the US 20% of cargo value as protection; Iran is demanding all ships use a northern route through its territorial waters and continues attacking ships in the US-protected Oman-hugging lane. Transit refinement vs the 07-17 note: 57 transits were recorded Fri-Sun (>50% wk/wk drop, vs ~130/day pre-war), and DOE says 8.5M bbl still transited Sunday with military assistance (total Gulf flows ~15M bpd) — heavily disrupted but not zero. ~25% of seaborne oil trade transits this chokepoint.
events.update_log_0723: 07-23: escalation widened — reports of attacks on tankers OFF THE SAUDI COAST (beyond Hormuz itself) and Trump renewed threats to intensify strikes on Iran; WTI +~3.8% to ~$90.14 (highest since June 8), Brent ~$98.44. The escalation vector is spreading regionally.
events.update_log_0726: 07-26 (weekend): Trump warned that each Iranian attack on a ship in the strait will be met with a US strike on an Iranian bridge or power plant, possibly near/within Tehran — a new infrastructure-targeting threat; Iran responded defiantly. Transits still ~6/day (Jul 18-19). ~27% of seaborne crude/products transit the strait. Talks remain stalled on the Hormuz-control sticking point. Watch the Sunday 6 PM ET reopen for a gap.
events.update_log_0728: 07-28: THE CLOSURE ITSELF HAS NOT CHANGED — severity held at 10/10. Trackers put the strait at day 148 closed. Traffic averaged ~10 ships/day 07-13 to 07-19 vs an ~88/day normal baseline; 15 transits on 07-19; the tanker queue off Kharg Island grew to 24 vessels on 07-26 from 21. What changed is the CONFLICT tempo around it, not the waterway. This event is deliberately left at its headline severity and damped downstream by the realized-capacity factor — see the 07-28 chokepoint_status observation (32%, confidence 0.55). Do not cut this event's severity to express de-escalation; that is the capacity component's job.
events.update_log_0729: 07-29: no reported change to the waterway itself - the 07-28 escalation hit Jordan and eastern Iraq, not Gulf shipping or energy infrastructure. No new vessel attack reported since the Kaifan on 07-20. Severity held at 10/10; the 07-28 capacity observation (32%, confidence 0.55) still stands and is now 1 day old.
events.update_log_0730: 07-30: MarineTraffic recorded at least 14 commercial transits in the prior 24 hours (8 inbound to the Gulf, 6 outbound to the Gulf of Oman) against a pre-war baseline of ~120 crossings per day - roughly 12% of normal traffic. Severity held at 10/10. The 07-29 US strikes hit Iranian COASTAL SURVEILLANCE, DEFENCE AND MARITIME CAPABILITIES at Bandar Abbas and Kish, i.e. the assets Iran uses to threaten the waterway. Near term that raises risk; over a longer horizon degrading those assets could REDUCE Iran's ability to keep the strait shut. Both readings are live; neither is scored as a capacity change until transits actually move.

events.description: Active military conflict between the US/Israel and Iran since late February 2026. 07-27 MATERIAL DE-ESCALATION: the two sides HALTED STRIKES against each other over the weekend — the US paused its attacks starting late Friday and Tehran halted retaliatory strikes — amid efforts to revive diplomacy. WTI fell ~5% to ~$84.83 and Brent ~4.7% to ~$92.27 on the news. This is a pause, not a settlement: the underlying conflict is unresolved and the strait remains shut, but the active-strike tempo that drove the July premium has stopped. Severity and supply impact cut accordingly (9/7 -> 7/5).
events.update_log_0728: 07-28: THE PAUSE HELD A SECOND DAY. No new US strikes; Tehran halted retaliation against US allies. US ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said Trump would give negotiations 'a little bit of room'; Trump said the US halted strikes at the regime's request and will resume if no ceasefire deal is reached. WTI extended losses ~3% to ~$80.11 (Sep contract), Brent ~$85.08-86.58. Severity cut 7 -> 6 and supply impact 5 -> 4: a second quiet day with no vessel attacks since the Kaifan on 07-20 is a real change in tempo, not just a headline. Caveat below in the talks event — Iran publicly denies negotiating with the US at all.
events.update_log_0729: 07-29 THE PAUSE BROKE. At 5:45 PM ET Tuesday the IRGC launched multiple ballistic missiles from Iran at US forces in an 'attempted surprise attack' (CENTCOM), targeting Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in JORDAN. All missiles were intercepted; no US deaths. The launch came roughly two hours after Netanyahu left a closed-door White House meeting with Trump - their first face-to-face since the war began 02-28. Separately, US and Saudi aircraft struck logistics and weapons sites across eastern Iraq. WTI reversed +4.4% to ~$82.73. The 48-hour pause reported 07-27/07-28 is over: severity 6 -> 8, supply impact 4 -> 6. Note this attack widened the geography again (Jordan, Iraq) without yet touching Gulf energy infrastructure.
events.update_log_0729_airdefense: 07-29 NEW STRUCTURAL RISK - interceptor depletion. Analysis reported 07-28 puts US Patriot stocks at 759-827, down from 2,330 pre-war (-65%), and THAAD at 234-278 from 452. US forces are now reported to be DELIBERATELY LETTING SOME IRANIAN MISSILES THROUGH where a strike is judged not to threaten American lives. CSIS estimates three years to replenish. This does not change today's supply picture but it materially fattens the left tail: the probability that a future Iranian salvo actually lands on energy infrastructure rises as the shield thins. Tracked as a risk driver, not scored as a supply disruption.
events.update_log_0730: 07-30 THE US RETALIATED - HEAVY WAVE. Trump said it was 'our turn'; CENTCOM completed a heavy wave of strikes at ~10 PM ET on 07-29 against DOZENS of IRGC targets: military command centres, missile and drone facilities, and - the part that matters for oil - COASTAL SURVEILLANCE AND DEFENCE SITES AND MARITIME CAPABILITIES. Explosions reported across southern Iran including BANDAR ABBAS and KISH ISLAND, both directly on the Strait of Hormuz. Jordan's military said it intercepted five of the Iranian missiles fired 07-28. Brent jumped ~7% to $90.66 on Trump's retaliation threat. Severity 6 -> 9, supply impact 4 -> 7. This is the highest tempo since the 07-23 peak.
events.update_log_0730_energy_restraint: 07-30 KEY RESTRAINT, EXPLICITLY SOURCED: Israel's Defence Minister said the US has been PREVENTING Israel from striking Iranian energy infrastructure over economic and energy concerns, and CENTCOM's 07-29 wave targeted military and IRGC positions - NOT energy infrastructure. This is the single most important bullish-tail limiter on the board: the escalation is severe but is being deliberately steered away from the barrels. If that restraint breaks, the escalation scenario repricing is immediate and large.

events.description: De-escalation diplomacy has shifted to Muscat: an Iranian delegation led by FM Araghchi visited Oman for talks on reopening the strait; France and Britain are studying Omani-drafted proposals for IMO-supervised navigational fees. Mediation channels are strained (Oman and Qatar both struck by Iran on 2026-07-12; Pakistan track suspended). Headlines around these talks whipsaw prices in both directions. 07-20: first de-escalation flicker — Iran said US talks 'could be pursued based on national interests,' and oil erased gains. 07-22 REVERSAL: the flicker died — Secretary of State Rubio said Iran is 'not serious' about peace talks and oil jumped ~4% (WTI to ~$87-88); it is now the 11th consecutive night of US strikes on Iran, and the toll/fee dispute over transit vessels is the stated sticking point. Talks path deteriorated, not advanced.
events.update_log_0727: 07-27: diplomacy REVIVING — the mutual strike pause over the weekend was explicitly framed as an effort to restart talks. This is the #1 invalidation-trigger direction for the bullish thesis: if it firms into a reopening framework, the remaining premium unwinds. Not yet a settlement; the strait is still shut and no shipping-capacity change has been reported.
events.update_log_0728: 07-28 CONTRADICTION ON THE RECORD — read this before treating the pause as a peace process. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said Monday that Iran 'currently have no negotiations with the United States' and that its only official talks are with OMAN, about the future of the strait. Washington simultaneously describes the pause as giving negotiations room. Both cannot be fully true. Confidence in the diplomatic track is therefore cut 0.8 -> 0.6 and severity held: the strike pause is verified (observable, two days of no strikes), the negotiation is not. Treat the pause as a military fact and the talks as an unconfirmed claim.
events.update_log_0729: 07-29: the diplomatic read from 07-27/07-28 is INVALIDATED by events. Iran's own MFA had already denied negotiating with the US (only with Oman); the 07-28 missile salvo at a US base in Jordan settles it. The 'pause for talks' framing was Washington's, not a mutual process. Confidence cut 0.6 -> 0.4 and status held at monitoring. The Oman channel on the strait itself has not been reported dead - that is the only live thread.
events.update_log_0730: 07-30: the talks track is effectively dead for now. Iran fired first on 07-28, the US completed a heavy retaliatory wave on 07-29, and Iran's MFA had already denied negotiating with Washington. Confidence cut 0.4 -> 0.25; status held at monitoring because the Oman channel on the strait has not been reported closed.

events.description: Unidentified drones struck four tankers at the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) marine terminal near Novorossiysk between 07-17 and 07-20, suspending loadings for a week. Kazakh oil and gas condensate output fell to ~1.0M bpd by 07-26. RESOLVED 07-27: CPC restarted crude intake and tanker loading (SEAMAJESTY and MILOS loading Tengizchevroil crude at two single-point moorings); operations continue subject to security assessment. This is a NON-HORMUZ supply channel returning — a bearish input independent of the Iran file, and part of why WTI extended losses on 07-28. Kazakhstan produced 45.7Mt in H1 2026, -8.4% y/y; full-year target cut to 98Mt.

chokepoint_status.summary: Transits collapsed to ~6 vessels/day vs 18-22 earlier in the month and ~130/day pre-war; US naval blockade in force and CENTCOM striking assets along the coast.

57 transits recorded Fri-Sun (~19/day, still >50% below the prior week) BUT DOE reports 8.5M bbl moved on Sunday alone with military escort against ~20M bpd normal Hormuz volume. Vessel-count and volume measures disagree (15% vs ~42%), so capacity is a blended estimate at moderate confidence.

First refresh since 07-19. Vessel-count leg confirmed and slightly worse: traffic averaged ~10 ships/day 07-13 to 07-19 against an ~88/day normal baseline (about 11%), with 15 transits on 07-19, and the tanker queue off Kharg Island grew to 24 vessels on 07-26 from 21 the day before - ships are waiting, not moving. The volume leg is unrefreshed: the last hard figure is DOE's 8.5M bbl on 07-19, now nine days old, so the blended 32% carries reduced confidence rather than a changed level. Military risk cut extreme -> high: no US or Iranian strikes for a second consecutive day and no vessel attacked since the Kuwaiti tanker Kaifan on 07-20. Insurance risk held at extreme - war-risk premiums have not been reported as repricing on a two-day pause. Supply impact bearish on the strike pause plus the CPC Black Sea terminal restart, not on any capacity improvement in the strait itself, which has not occurred.

Fresh vessel-count data: MarineTraffic recorded at least 14 commercial transits in the prior 24 hours - 8 inbound to the Persian Gulf, 6 outbound to the Gulf of Oman - against a pre-war baseline of roughly 120 crossings per day, about 12% of normal traffic. That is consistent with, and slightly worse than, the 07-28 vessel leg. The volume leg is still unrefreshed since DOE's 8.5M bbl figure of 07-19, now eleven days old, so the blended estimate ticks 32 to 30 with confidence cut 0.55 to 0.50 rather than the level moving sharply. Military risk restored high to extreme: CENTCOM completed a heavy wave of strikes late 07-29 against dozens of IRGC targets explicitly including coastal surveillance, coastal defence and maritime capabilities, with explosions reported at Bandar Abbas and Kish Island - both directly on the strait. Insurance risk held at extreme. Supply impact flips bearish to bullish on the resumption of active hostilities, though note the US is reported to be restraining Israel from striking Iranian energy infrastructure and the 07-29 wave did not target it.
